In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the peritrophic membrane (PM) of Simulium (Diptera, Simuliidae) in the adult stage.
the structure, function, and formation of the peritrophic membrane in the adult simuliid, a blood-sucking fly.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peritrophic membranes of simuliids are formed in the posterior part of their posterior midgut.
the peritrophic membranes of the adult Simuliidae are secretions of the posterior midguts, formed in situ and not derived from the pharate adults, and are not secreted in response to blood ingestion.
the peritrophic membranes of adult female simuliids, before and after blood feeding, are formed in the posterior part of their midguts, and that they have a role in the process of digestion of blood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the peritrophic membranes of adult Simuliids are formed in the posterior part of midgut, are of the same general type, and are formed and disappear according to a common pattern, but that there are species differences in the rate of formation and the number of laminae, and that these differences are related to the rate of blood digestion.

the adult peritrophic membrane is formed by the posterior midguts, that it is a product of the digestive process, and that it is not a product of the pharates or a secretion from the anterior midguts.

the peritrophic membranes of simuliids are not secreted by a specialized cell, but are formed by the action of a secretion from the posterior midguts of adults and pharate adults on a blood meal or blood meal substitute.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peritrophic matrix of adult female Simuliids (blackflies) is a dynamic structure, and that the peritrophin-like proteins (PPLPs) are the major structural components.
the peritrophic membranes of the pharates and adults of simuliids are not formed in response to blood feeding.
the peritrophic matrix is a highly dynamic structure that is constantly being remodeled in response to changes in the environment.
